title: Screen ceramic finishing media from finished metal washers
objective: Pour a dry mixture of full-scale metal washers and ceramic angle-cut cylinders into a supported manual separating screen, use the screen to recover the media in the receiver while retaining every washer, then release the screen onto its supports.
skills: Bimanual rim grasping and load sharing
Controlled pouring into a supported screen
Bridge-clearing through bounded tilt and agitation
Stable tool placement and collision-free release
success_conditions: Let F be the fraction of starting mixture mass that has physically entered the screen, and r the current receiver-contained media mass divided by starting media mass. Before a permanent failure, score = 0.20F + 0.70 min(max(r/0.98,0),1) + 0.10D. D becomes 1 only after F=1, r>=0.98, every washer remains in the screen, the screen rests on its supports, both grippers are at least 60 mm clear, and fresh observations continuously satisfy those conditions for 3.0 seconds; any broken prerequisite resets the dwell. Thus 98–100% recovery earns all 70 recovery points. A washer leaving the screen, deliberate workpiece removal, or receiver contamination permanently sets the score to zero. Media crossing the rim, contacting the floor, or escaping the receiver is immutable loss and cannot earn recovery credit; any such event also prevents D. Washer fracture or permanent deformation caps the score at 0.40. Full score requires F=1, r>=0.98, all washers retained, no spill, loss, contamination, or damage, and the released dwell. Continuous video and before/after weighing can check the outcome; motion style, shake count, hand identity, and action order are not graded.
industrial_value: Raytech identifies manual screens as equipment for separating manufactured parts from finishing media, while its guidance warns that excessive separation motion can damage uncushioned parts. The objective represents a real post-finishing recovery operation affecting production workers, inspectors, and material handlers rather than appearance-based sorting.
dexterity: The source fixes a nominal 1/2-inch screen class and 9.525 × 22.225 mm angle-cut media. In the representative model, the clear apertures are explicitly assumed to be 12.7 mm squares: the media diameter can fit, but its length exceeds the approximately 17.96 mm aperture diagonal. Native controls must demonstrate end-first passage, transverse bridging, and bridge release. The robot must pour into the supported screen, establish a coordinated two-arm grasp, mobilize bridged media without throwing it over the rim, retain annular steel workpieces, and reseat and release the loaded screen.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, ceramic media product list
FAQ, “What is the best way to separate the parts from the media?”

asset_plan: Build an independently authored, representative full-scale screen using the sourced 368.3 mm outer diameter and 63.5 mm depth. Treat the following as frozen, testable modeling assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD: 12.7 mm clear square apertures, 3 mm ribs and rib thickness, 15.7 mm pitch, 150 mm flat perforated-floor radius, 3 mm sloped wall, and 0.40 kg screen mass. Preserve true openings with finite compound bars or supported non-convex collision; never use a convex hull that fills the holes. Model 24 free ceramic bodies at the sourced 9.525 × 22.225 mm envelope, with assumed parallel 15-degree angle cuts and 2500 kg/m³ density; compute and record each realized closed-mesh mass and inertia, with about 3.50 g as the analytic reference. Model four disclosed representative plain carbon-steel washers, not a claimed commercial SKU: 30 mm OD, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thickness, 7850 kg/m³, approximately 20.62 g each. Use initial uncalibrated contact assumptions of ceramic/polymer static/dynamic friction 0.50/0.35, steel/polymer 0.45/0.35, media/media 0.40/0.30, restitution 0.05, 0.15 mm contact offset, zero rest offset, and 32/8 solver position/velocity iterations. Provide a rigid receiver, two physical supports, and a 78 mm OD gripper-accessible feed cup. Before robot integration, verify at physics-substep resolution: end-first media passage; transverse bridging and motion-driven release; washer retention in every relevant orientation; whether angle-cut noses can enter or lodge in the washer’s 8 mm bore despite the 9.525 mm body diameter; no boundary aperture larger than specified; no-op, gravity, spill, and aggressive-motion controls. Then verify actual YAM contacts and joint/body traces for cup pouring, bimanual lift and sifting, support placement, 60 mm release clearance, and fresh 3-second dwell. Keep component physics metrics separate from task scoring.
risk: The 368.3 mm screen is large relative to the pinned 0.8 × 1.2 m tabletop, so bimanual rim reach, feed-cup access, support clearance, and loaded grasp stability remain construction risks. Slender media may tunnel or self-lock unrealistically, and angle-cut tips may lodge in washer bores. These are explicit native component gates: failure blocks full-scene development but does not leave the mechanism undefined. Material and contact values are disclosed uncalibrated assumptions and must not be tuned with hidden forces, collision removal, particle freezing, or velocity caps that suppress genuine spills.
